atmosphere_grid_note: Both components (5340K, 5185K) fall below the previous grid floor (5750K); needed ckp00_5000.fits and ckp00_5250.fits, downloaded 2026-08-27. ckp00_5500.fits was also added 2026-08-27 after the first post-download run failed with 'Initial guess is outside of provided bounds': the primary component's literature Teff (5340K) sits above the 5000-5250K bracket originally listed here (which only bracketed the secondary's 5185K), so the grid must extend to 5500K to bracket both components. fixed_parameters_note: Radius is pinned at its literature value rather than freed alongside Teff1/Teff2/E(B-V): Table 4 of the same reference supplies 10 real entire-system measurements (Johnson U/B/V/R, Stromgren u/v/b/y, Tycho BT/VT) for this system, which is formally enough degrees of freedom to free all 5 photometric parameters (Teff1, Teff2, R1, R2, E(B-V)). Freeing all 5 was tested (2026-08-27) even with the full 10-band dataset and still collapsed to a non-physical solution (one radius pinned at its lower optimizer bound, the other driven to ~2x its literature value) with a far worse chi-square than the 3-free-parameter fit. This confirms the earlier 4-measurement finding was a genuine degeneracy in unresolved-binary photometric SED fitting, not a data-starvation artifact: an unresolved combined-light SED alone cannot uniquely separate two stars' individual (Teff, R) pairs, no matter how many bands are added, because each star's broadband flux depends on Teff and R only through the combination R^2*Teff^4-ish integrated over the passband -- a genuine physical degeneracy axis that only breaks with an independent constraint on radius (e.g. a dynamical-mass + mass-radius relation, or interferometry), which is exactly why the real Al-Wardat method combines SED fitting with evolutionary-track/isochrone cross-checks rather than fitting radius from photometry alone. See docs/project_decisions.md for the full investigation, including the Sun-at-10pc pipeline calibration check that ruled out a synthetic-photometry code bug before reaching this conclusion.

excluded_measurements.note: Excluded 2026-08-27: the SVO Filter Profile Service 'Generic/Stromgren.u' Vega-system zero point (3.2441e-9 erg/s/cm2/A) was found to disagree with this system's measured Stromgren u magnitude by ~1.7 mag -- a factor of ~4.7x in flux -- far outside the ~0.25-0.5 mag systematic offset seen consistently across every other band (Johnson U/B/V/R, Stromgren v/b/y, Tycho BT/VT). The same ~1-1.5 mag anomaly, specific to Stromgren u, also showed up independently in a Sun-at-10pc pipeline sanity check. This points to the classical Stromgren uvbybeta system's u-band zero point (as originally calibrated by Crawford & Barnes 1970 against a specific set of standard stars) being offset from a naive Vega-spectrum convolution in a well-documented, system-specific way that a simple SVO Vega zero point does not capture -- not a bug in this pipeline's flux scaling (verified correct via the same Sun-at-10pc check, and via Johnson/Tycho bands all matching literature to <0.1 mag). Excluded from fitting pending a properly-calibrated Stromgren-system zero point; retained here as a documented, sourced literature value for future work.
